newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN MINFINS ALMOST UNCHANGED, WATCH U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN MINFINS ALMOST UNCHANGED, WATCH U.S. DATA.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices were unchanged as the market awaited the U.S. July and July producer price index, which will determine the trend for the next few days, dealers said on Wednesday.
The bonds were almost unchanged in healthy volumes as a morning slip after a fall in U.S. Treasuries was compensated by short-position covering later.
"It is unlikely that anyone will do anything serious before the figures are issued," ING Barings dealer Maxim Arkhipov said.

The market expects the figure will indicate that the U.S. economy was growing strongly and inflation pressures are building up, which would prompt investors to sell debt including MinFins, dealers said.
According to a Reuters poll, economists forecast the July PPI would be 0.1 percent after -0.1 percent in June, and they expect a year-on-year figure of 0.4 percent after -0.1 percent.
Dealers differed on how strongly MinFins would fall if the forecasts turned out to be true.

"If the figures are bad, I am afraid everything will drop sharply, as very many Western investors have big long-term positions," Arkhipov said. "If they start selling, it will be a serious hit for the market."
But Natsionalny Rezervny Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said the fall would not be a deep one.
"I think there are short positions in MinFins to be covered after the figures are released, so MinFins will not fall strongly," he said.

He said investors in MinFins were also watching the process of Russia's debt reconciliation to the London Club of commercial bank-creditors and expected an upgrade of Russia's international credit rating soon.
These two factors will cushion the fall, he said.
